newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's king gives freed dissident a lift home.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's king gives freed dissident a lift home.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein personally gave his fiercest critic a lift home from prison after ordering his release on Friday, raising opposition hopes on Saturday for further amnesties for political detainees.
"The king drove Laith (Shubailat) in his car from Swaqa prison to his mother's home," Rima Shubailat told Reuters.

Shubailat, head of the Islamist-dominated engineers' union and vocal critic of Jordan's 1994 peace treaty with Israel, was sentenced in March to three years in prison on charges of "violating the king's dignity" after branding him a traitor.

"Sure I am happy, thank God, but my happiness will only be complete if the rest of the political detainees are released and there will be a breakthrough into an atmosphere of freedoms... then my happiness will be consolidated," Shubailat told Reuters from his Amman home on Saturday.
He declined to comment on his ride from jail with the king.
Family members said King Hussein drove Shubailat in his car from the prison gates of Swaqa, the country's biggest prison complex, to an emotional reunion with his mother.

Political analysts say the king is a master of co-opting political adversaries who plotted against him during his four decades on the throne with many former opponents becoming members of his administration.
Opposition figures on Saturday welcomed Shubailat's release.

"We hope this release will be a prelude to the release of all the other political detainees and that it will be the start of a breakthrough in public liberties to put an end to the escalation of arrests we have seen recently," deputy Hamza Mansour, the spokesman of the Islamic Action Front (IAF).

Mansour, whose opposition party holds 16 seats in Jordan's 80-seat lower house of parliament, said the government arrested more dissidents since bread riots in August than over a whole decade of martial law before restoration of parliament in 1989.

Shubailat, a former parliamentary deputy, was sentenced to death in 1992 for trying to overthrow the government. He was pardoned the same year, but has maintained a strident opposition to the king's policies.

He spent late Friday and Saturday receiving scores of well-wishers at his Marj al-Hamam home outside Amman, including prominent opposition deputies and tribal members from his home town of Tafila in southern Jordan, family members said.

Opposition sources said the king's surprising move was part of government efforts to improve the political climate after civil disturbances broke out last August in the poorer south of the country following an increase in bread prices.

They said the release was also prompted by bad publicity over allegations by a local human rights group of widespread arrests and torture of political detainees. The government has denied the allegations.
The king said in a letter to Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti that Shubailat's eight months behind bars were enough punishment.
